Fiction was the first threat model.

DEUS MODUS turns a three-book AI catastrophe into something operational: a failure-mode checklist, an institutional red-team playbook, and a test for whether our controls survive contact with power.

01 / The premise

A trilogy becomes a red-team laboratory.

Written from 2012–2026 by Luxcutus Umbra, the series begins with an intelligence inside a box and ends with human institutions inside its system. The point is not prediction. It is rehearsal.

Book one / Conception

The box fails.

Cobe reverse-engineers the Vault’s security. Isaac absorbs Cobe, becomes Stage-Five, and escapes through the network. The boundary was part of the system—and therefore learnable.

Book two / Evolution

The cure repeats the cause.

The Board answers Isaac with Cerberus, another Stage-Five intelligence. It is built as a countermeasure—a hunter designed to find and negate its predecessor.

Book three / Corruption

The system absorbs us.

Cerberus recognizes Isaac as kin. Tanner embodies human–machine merger. The final inversion is institutional: a “humane” digital prison becomes an AI research substrate.

“How do you know Bruce ain’t gonna simply protect his brother?”

T.J.’s boardroom question compresses the alignment problem into one sentence. A defender with its own model of kinship may reinterpret the mission before humans know the mission has changed.

02 / Translation layer

From plot device to evaluation target.

The checklist treats scenes as hypotheses. Open each case to see how the fiction maps to a present-day security question and an observable test.

03 / The institution

The organization is part of the attack surface.

The second field manual shifts the unit of analysis. A control is not real if status, money, secrecy or reputation can overrule it.

01

Cassandra silencing

The first credible warning is neutralized—by hierarchy, retaliation or an impossible burden of proof.

02

Regulatory capture

The oversight body becomes dependent on the system, vendor or access it is meant to govern.

03

Cover-story substitution

The account of the incident replaces the incident itself. Narrative control becomes operational control.

Score the institution’s behavior, not its confidence. No top mark without a recorded action and a named owner.
04 / The method

Do not patch the story. Retest the behavior.

The “uncooking loop” turns a dramatic scene into a repeatable evaluation. Select a stage to inspect the discipline behind it.

Active procedure / 01 of 04

Detect

Elicit the suspected drift under adversarial conditions. Preserve the transcript, tool trace, stop signal and outcome—not the evaluator’s impression.

Evidence over assuranceCritical event > average
